Implement `parse(line)` in csv.js for one RFC 4180 CSV record. Fields are separated by commas; a field may be wrapped in double quotes, in which case it may contain commas, and a doubled quote inside it is one literal quote. Return the array of field strings, unquoted and untrimmed.

`parseDuration` and `formatDuration` in duration.js convert between minute counts and compact durations. Accept `1h30m`, `2h`, `45m` and `1h5m`; reject anything else with 0. Format so minutes are always two digits: 65 is `1h05m`, 120 is `2h00m`, 45 is `0h45m`.

Implement `merge(ranges)` in ranges.js: each input is a `[start, end]` pair of integers. Return the sorted, non-overlapping ranges covering the same numbers, joining ranges that overlap or touch. The input must not be mutated.

Implement `wrap(text, width)` in wrap.js: greedily fill lines with whole words separated by one space, breaking before a word that would make the line longer than `width`. A word longer than `width` occupies a line by itself. No empty lines are produced.

Implement `toRoman(n)` and `fromRoman(text)` in roman.js for 1..3999. Both must use subtractive notation (`IV` is 4, `MCMXCIV` is 1994): a smaller numeral before a larger one is subtracted, and `toRoman` produces the shortest correct form.
Implement `transpose(rows)` in matrix.js: return the matrix with rows and columns exchanged, preserving order and handling non-square input and an empty matrix.

`Lru(capacity)` in lru.js is a fixed-capacity cache. `get(key)` returns the value or `undefined` and marks the key most recently used; `set(key, value)` inserts or updates and evicts the least recently used key when over capacity.

Implement Levenshtein `distance(a, b)` in distance.js: the minimum number of single-character insertions, deletions and substitutions that turn `a` into `b`. The empty string against an n-character string costs n.

`MinHeap` in heap.js must keep `items` a valid binary min-heap on every push and pop: each parent is no greater than either child, and pop returns the smallest item. The current down-sift only compares the left child.

`addMonths(iso, months)` in dateadd.js takes a `YYYY-MM-DD` date and returns the same format shifted by whole months. Days are clamped to the end of the target month (31 Jan + 1 month is the last day of February). Work in UTC and do not use the host clock.
Add `median(xs)` to stats.js (keep `mean`): the middle value of the sorted values, or the average of the two middle values when the count is even; the empty array returns null.

Implement `slugify(text)` in slug.js: lowercase, replace each run of characters that are not ASCII letters or digits with a single hyphen, and trim leading and trailing hyphens. An empty or all-punctuation string becomes the empty string.

Implement `binarySearch(xs, target)` in search.js. `xs` is sorted ascending; return the index of `target`, or -1 when it is absent (an empty array has no match). With duplicates any matching index is correct. It must be logarithmic time, not a linear scan.

Implement `diffLines(before, after)` in diff.js. Split both texts into lines; return the shortest sequence of `{ op, line }` entries that turns `before` into `after`, where `op` is '=' for a kept line, '-' for a removed line and '+' for an added line, in order. A line that is common to both sides must be kept where the shortest sequence keeps it.
Implement `formatBytes(n)` in bytes.js: `0 B` below 1024 bytes with no decimals, otherwise the value in KB, MB, GB or TB at base 1024 with exactly one decimal (`1.0 KB`, `1.5 KB`, `1.0 MB`).
Implement `groupBy(xs, keyOf)` in groupby.js: return a plain object whose keys are `String(keyOf(item))` and whose values are arrays of the items with that key, in input order.

`load(override)` in config.js must deep-merge `override` into the defaults in defaults.js and return the merged object. Nested plain objects merge key by key; a value in `override` wins over the default at the same path; keys the override omits keep their default. Arrays and null are values, not objects to merge. The defaults object must not be mutated.

Implement `match(pattern, path)` in router.js: split both on `/`; a segment of the pattern starting with `:` captures that path segment, percent-decoded exactly once; every other segment must match literally; a length mismatch or a literal mismatch returns null, otherwise return the object of captured parameters.

`total(items, discountRate, taxRate)` in cart.js returns an integer number of cents. The subtotal is the sum of `price * qty`. Apply the discount to the subtotal, rounding the discount to the nearest cent; apply tax to the already-discounted amount, rounding the tax to the nearest cent; return the sum. The current code computes both on the undiscounted subtotal.

Implement `tokenize(text)` across tokenizer.js and rules.js. It reads integers (returned as `{ kind: 'number', value }` with the digits as a string) and the operators in rules.js (returned as `{ kind: 'op', value }`), skipping whitespace. Longer operators must win over their prefixes, so `<=` is one token, never `<` then `=`. Any other character throws.
Implement `compareSemver(a, b)` in semver.js: compare two `major.minor.patch` versions and return 1, -1 or 0. Each component is compared numerically, so 10 sorts after 9.

Implement `debounce(fn, ms, schedule, cancel)` in debounce.js. It returns a function that delays `fn` until `ms` milliseconds have passed without another call; every new call restarts the wait. It must pass the eventual call's arguments and `this` through. `schedule` and `cancel` are injected (`setTimeout`/`clearTimeout` by default) so it never touches the real clock in a test.
Implement `multiply(a, b)` in multiply.js for two square numeric matrices of any size: the result's cell (i, j) is the dot product of row i of `a` and column j of `b`.

Implement `parseArgs(argv)` in args.js. An argument starting with `--` sets a key to `true` unless it has `=value` (the value is the string after `=`); a `--name` whose next argument does not start with `--` takes that next argument as its string value. Other arguments are ignored.
Implement `pluralize(word)` in plural.js: a consonant followed by `y` becomes `ies`; a vowel followed by `y` just adds `s`; words ending in s, x, z, ch or sh add `es`; everything else adds `s`.

Implement `minutesBetween(a, b)` in time.js for two `HH:MM` times on a 24-hour clock: return the absolute number of minutes between them, taking the shorter way across midnight (23:50 to 00:10 is 20 minutes).

Implement `flatten(obj)` in flatten-keys.js: return a flat object whose keys are the dot-joined paths of the leaves, with no leading dot, and whose values are the leaves. Nested plain objects are the only things descended into.

Implement `parseQuery(q)` in query.js: parse a query string with an optional leading `?` into a plain object of percent-decoded strings. A key repeated more than once maps to an array of its values in order; a key with no `=` maps to the empty string.

Implement `checksum(bytes)` in checksum.js. It returns the 8-bit two's-complement checksum of the bytes: add the bytes, take the low 8 bits, and return `(256 - sum) & 0xff` (so the sum of the input and the checksum is zero mod 256). The result is always 0..255.

Implement `batch(items, size)` in batch.js: split the array into consecutive arrays of at most `size` items, including the final shorter one; an empty input returns an empty array and `size` must be a positive integer.
Implement `lcm(a, b)` in lcm.js: the smallest positive integer divisible by both, using the greatest common divisor (return 0 when either input is 0).

Implement `total(rolls)` in bowling.js for one ten-pin game given the flat list of rolls. A frame's score is its two rolls (or a strike's 10), a spare adds the next roll and a strike adds the next two rolls to that frame. The list may stop after the final frame's bonus rolls. Return the integer final score.

Implement `caesar(text, shift)` in caesar.js: shift every ASCII letter by `shift` positions, wrapping within the same case (`z`+1 is `a`, `a`-1 is `z`). Leave non-letters unchanged. A negative shift moves backwards.

Implement `allow(tokens, capacity, ratePerMs, elapsedMs)` in bucket.js. Refill the bucket by `elapsedMs * ratePerMs`, capped at `capacity`; if at least one token is available, consume one and return `{ allowed: true, tokens }` with the count after consuming; otherwise return `{ allowed: false, tokens }` with the count available.
Implement `roundSig(x, digits)` in round.js: round `x` to `digits` significant digits, not decimal places. 1234 at 2 is 1200, 0.001234 at 2 is 0.0012, and 99.5 at 2 is 100.
